# Actual CSS

> Plain CSS component framework for new projects: semantic classes, shared variants, small tokens, theme hooks, and progressive enhancement.

Actual CSS uses a small public grammar: `.component [intent] [variant] [size] [modifier]`. It claims unprefixed class names by design. Existing projects with collisions should use cascade layers, import order, or an application-side prefix transform.

## Documentation

- [Documentation source](docs/pages/): the docs pages, generated into `site/` by `bun run build:docs` (start at `site/index.html`).

## Package Entrypoints

`package.json#exports` is the canonical package surface.

- `actual-css/css` — the source core, the recommended starting point: tokens, theme contract, reset, base elements, and universal variants. Components and layout primitives are NOT included; add them with `actual-css/css/<family>` or `actual-css/css/<family>/<module>`.
- `actual-css` / `actual-css/full` — the complete compiled framework, for zero-config and CDN use: core plus every component, form, layout, typography, effect, and utility family.
- `actual-css/js` — the enhancement-loader entry only: it watches `data-enhance-modules` manifest blocks and imports the declared enhancers on demand.
- `actual-css/js/full` — the complete runtime with all built-in enhancers pre-registered.
- `actual-css/reserved-classes.json` — machine-readable list of the framework-owned class namespace. Use it to check whether a class belongs to Actual CSS and to validate claimed framework classes; application-specific classes are expected to exist outside this manifest.
- `actual-css/components.json` — machine-readable component index, derived from the sources (CSS headers, selectors, package exports, `src/js`) by `scripts/build-catalog.js` and verified by `check:catalog`. Gives each component its import paths, owned classes, hooks, states, and registered enhancement tokens — enough to know what exists and where to read more, not a replacement for `docs/pages/components/*.md`.
- [Starter agent skill](skills/actual-css/SKILL.md) — a copyable skill for building with Actual CSS (vocabulary, hooks, layouts, enhancements); consuming projects extend it with a local `PROJECT.md`.
- Individual families and modules are importable separately (`actual-css/css/components`, `actual-css/css/layout/grid`, `actual-css/js/dialog`, …); see [README](README.md) and [Modular imports](docs/pages/guides/modular-import.md).

Forms are the one family with two aggregate entrypoints:
`actual-css/css/forms` is the native-control baseline; use
`actual-css/css/forms/all` for the complete forms family.

The composition guides in [README](README.md) and [Progressive Enhancements](docs/pages/enhancements/overview.md)
show supported CSS modules and individual enhancer imports without duplicating
the full export list here.

Presentation (`class`) and behavior are separate layers. `data-enhance` takes
four tokens only — `tabs`, `flyout`, `scrollspy`, `validation`; leaf behaviors
use their own attribute (`data-tooltip`, `data-mask`, `data-filter`,
`data-context-menu`) and `<dialog>` needs none. See
[when a token, when a data-*](docs/design-notes/enhancement-contract.md).

Behaviour primitives are independently importable for building custom widgets,
including `enhance`, `surface`, `floating`, `focus-group`, `keys`, `input`,
`command`, `menu`, `focus`, `escape`, and `events`. See
[widget primitives](docs/design-notes/widget-primitives.md).

## What the vocabulary does not have

- No compound intent classes (`.btn-primary`, `.badge-success`): intents and
  variants are separate classes on the component (`.btn primary outline`).
- No breakpoint or state prefixes (`md:stack`, `hover:…`) and no arbitrary
  values: layout primitives and container queries own responsiveness.
- No spacing scale (`mt-4`, `p-2`): spacing comes from `--gap`, density
  (`.compact`, `.spacious`), and component hooks.
- `is-*` classes are written by the runtime, not by authors.
- Modifiers such as `.ghost`, `.link`, `.flush`, `.raised` only mean something
  on their component; alone they are inert.

See [naming](docs/design-notes/naming.md) and
[utilities non-goals](docs/pages/utilities/overview.md#non-goals).

## Choosing a page shell

Before choosing a content layout, choose the page shell:

- Normal scrolling page, marketing/editorial site, or ordinary application page
  → semantic landmarks; optionally `.app-shell` and `.navbar`.
- Persistent topbar + independently scrolling main + adaptive bottom/side
  primary navigation → `.app-layout`.

Do not choose `.app-layout` merely because the product is an application. Its
viewport-sized shell, internal scrolling, and adaptive navigation are one
combined contract. See [layout choices](docs/pages/layout/choosing.md).

## Choosing a layout primitive

Pick from the relationship between children, not the number of children in one mockup:

- Responsive collection of cards/items where an incomplete final row is acceptable → `.grid`
- Known structural density, at most N columns → `.grid-N`
- Peer regions that must switch together → `.switcher`
- Main content plus a secondary region (content + aside) → `.sidebar-layout`
- Fixed media followed by flexible content → `.media`
- Explicit region placement on a shared 12-column canvas → `.column-layout`
- Vertical flow → `.stack`; wrapping inline items → `.cluster`

`.container-query` establishes the framework's shared
`actual-container / inline-size` container for components that explicitly
respond to allocated space; it is not a general prerequisite for responsive
layouts.

Use `--grid-columns` on `.grid` for exact track templates that do not match a
built-in layout contract: arbitrary structural counts (seven calendar days),
asymmetric fractional tracks, or mixed intrinsic/flexible tracks. See
[Choosing a layout](docs/pages/layout/choosing.md).

`.status-bar` is transient feedback only; persistent metrics or application
state belong in normal content such as cards, badges and alerts.

## Before generating application CSS

Read [Building with Actual CSS](docs/pages/guides/integrating-actual-css.md)
before writing application styles.

1. Start with Actual's vocabulary: theme tokens, then layout primitives, then components, then their public hooks, then small utilities, then application CSS.
2. Choose layout primitives by relationship, not item count.
3. Prefer component/layout hooks over replacement rules (tune before replacing).
4. Search the class manifest before inventing generic utilities.
5. Keep literal palette colors inside the theme/token block; derive decorative colors from tokens.
6. Use application CSS for genuinely product-specific styling — brand marks, unusual geometry, bespoke animation.

The goal is no duplicated framework behavior and no palette literals outside the
token layer, not zero application CSS.
